In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "square root" operation preserves regularity for formal power languages if and only if the underlying semiring has a zero, is commutative, and is locally finite.
the "square root" operation preserves rationality of formal power series if and only if the underlying semiring satisfies both the local finiteness and the commutativity conditions.
the square root operation preserves rationality for commutative and locally finite semirings, while it does not preserve rationality for general semirings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the square-root operation preserves rationality for the formal power series over commutative or non-commutative locally finite semirings, and the square operation preserves rationality over non-commutative semirings.

the rationality of formal power series can always be preserved by "square-root" and "square" operations, while the rationality of the formal power series obtained by "cube-root" and "cubing" operations can only be preserved in the commutative or the locally finite case, and not in general.

, in general, the "root" operation does not preserve rationality, the "power" operation preserves rationality for commutative or finite semirings, and the "square-root", "cube-root", and "root" operations preserve rationality for locally finite semirings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theory of formal power series can serve as a unifying framework for the study of codings of formal language and formal power series.

the formal power series framework is more powerful in capturing and generalizing the behavior of the transformations than the formal language framework, as the formal language framework is a special case of the formal power series.
formal power series provide a rich setting to investigate transformations of formal languages, and we hope that the results of this paper will motivate more research in this direction.
